sections.body: A concept page could synthesize methods that spend rendering work where viewers are most sensitive. The motion-quality model allocates resolution and refresh rate using spatial resolution, refresh rate, velocity, predictability, blur, and judder; foveated rendering allocates spatial quality using visual-acuity and contrast-sensitivity limits in the human visual system.
sections.heading: Section 1

sections.body: The shared idea is not simply lowering quality to save time, but predicting which degradations remain perceptually acceptable. Evidence is strongest for motion-adaptive refresh/resolution and foveated regional quality, while links to broader perceptual temporal coherence are more general.
sections.heading: Section 2

title: Perceptual Quality Allocation Under Rendering Budgets
